<!-- pr-reviewer: 367f481856d59455d809a6082fca25b7a3e8e56b -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Reviewed at the safety tier; the PR author is a collaborator and this is a review by an agent that did not write the change.)

**What looks good**
- Every cache is keyed by the input itself, so no hand-bumped counter can go stale: `features_of_shared` and `resolve_chain` key on the allocation of the facet `Arc` / `Arc<Features>` (a held `Weak` keeps the address from being reused; any `set_facets` landing, which undo and redo also go through, is a new key), and `pocket_region_memo` compares the whole input (loops, part facets, planes, unit) for equality. A changed unit or setup alignment changes the facets or planes passed in, so it misses. A selection change changes the loops or chain ids, so it misses.
- `frame_memo::scene_scope` lives for one `world::collect` only, under an immutable borrow of the state, is dropped on every exit (unwind included), and is never read outside a scope.
- Pick results, stitch results and cut geometry are unchanged: the `feature::resolve_chain` to `model::resolve_chain` change is a signature ripple, the memo calls the same function, and errors other than `Invalid`/`Empty` are never cached. No post, goldens or toolpath code is touched; `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `recorded_post_streams` and `posting` pass unchanged.
- No unwrap/expect outside tests, counters use `saturating_add`, no new `camcraft-*` dependency, provenance lines and a decision file are present.
- Pins: `selection_frame_cost::frames_without_a_change_walk_digest_and_slice_nothing` (10 still frames, zero walks, digests and slices, one region build per scene) and `a_selection_change_or_a_landing_is_a_new_answer` (new selection and a `set_facets` landing recompute, the drawn region equals a fresh compute, later frames are still), plus the unit pins in `chain_memo` and `pocket_memo`.

**Results, merged with main (`2ac91e73b`... trial merge of NeoTech/Camcraft main at review time), run locally on host dude (the runner API is not readable with this token)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 355 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- 35 app test binaries the diff maps to (area_*, pocket_*, slot_*, feature*, pick*, stitch_cross, probe_pick, golden_cl, posting, recorded_post_streams, solid_law_goldens, mcp_pick, mcp_pockets, commands_undo, wire_contour, align_axes, points_align, plane_align_edges and the rest of the author's list): 299 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`): 965 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored, including both pins.
- Clippy `-D warnings`: clean for `camcraft-app` (lib, lib tests, bins) and `camcraft-ui --all-targets`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets` does not compile on `crates/app/tests/wire_tool.rs:106-107` (`CuttingRow` missing `stepdown`/`stepover`, `material` expected `Option<WorkMaterial>`). The PR does not touch that file or `CuttingRow`; it is a break on main, not this PR. It needs its own issue if there is none.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans all 252 steps for this diff (it touches `model.rs`), so I ran the author's touched binaries instead, as the PR body did.

**Not exercised here**
- The GPU frame time and the `~/repro/fig8.camproj` hand check (the maintainer's own hand test in the PR comment says selecting edges performs well). I did not measure a selection with many chains after #2215 beyond the 4-run and 8-10 chain headless cases the PR reports.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. `model/geometry.rs` memo: dead meshes keep their allocation until the next call prunes them (a held `Weak` keeps the block). Bounded at 32 entries; harmless.
2. `pocket_region_memo` compares the part's facets by value on each hit (O(triangles) per call, once per scene thanks to `scene_scope`). Cheap next to a slice, but if it ever shows up, an `Arc` allocation key like the other two is the fix.
3. Caches are thread-local: a headless MCP/CLI thread keeps its own, with no stale risk, only separate hit rates.
4. `selection.rs`, `interact.rs`, `model.rs` were already over 400 lines; this adds one to a few lines each.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
